chunks.fa: Welcome back to the channel, today we learn Spanish at the market

chunks.voc: bueno good, pl. buenos; día day, m. though it ends in -a — buenos días is the fixed greeting and is always plural
pone you put, formal (poner · pres. pongo · pret. puso · to put (p.p. puesto; fut. pondré)); me pone, lit. do you put me, is how one asks a shopkeeper for something
naranja orange, f.; the question mark opens as well as closes, and only the question is inside it
cuánto how much, with the accent every question word carries; cuestan they cost (costar · pres. cuesto · pret. costó · to cost), the o breaking to ue under the stress
están they are (estar · pres. estoy · pret. estuvo · to be — estar: where and how it is right now (place, state, the result of a change)), of a price here; ser would be for what a thing is
el kilo the kilo — Spanish says the where English says a
señora madam; ñ is the ny of canyon
vale all right — in Spain, the everyday yes
me llevo I will take (llevarse · pres. me llevo · pret. se llevó · to take away with one); the ll is said like the y of yes
aquí here, the qu said k with the u silent; tiene you have, formal (tener · pres. tengo · pret. tuvo · to have (fut. tendré)) — aquí tiene is here you are
hasta until; luego later — the ordinary goodbye
mucho much, pl. muchas agreeing with gracias, which is feminine and plural
bueno shortened to buen before a masculine singular noun; día day, m.
